# **2\. Overall Description** {#2.-overall-description}

## **2.1 Product Perspective** {#2.1-product-perspective}

Kitchen406 is a new web-based platform developed specifically for the operations of Kitchen406, a home-based bakery in Metro Cebu. It centralizes processes currently handled through messages, spreadsheets, physical records, and manual monitoring into one system for customer transactions and bakery operations.

The platform consists of a customer-facing Web Storefront, an Owner-Admin Dashboard, and a restricted Staff Interface that use the same underlying product, order, inventory, and scheduling data. It also integrates with external services for QR Ph payments, location services, delivery, notifications, and image storage. The current design specifically separates customer, administrator, and staff access while keeping their information within the same platform.

## **2.2 Product Functions** {#2.2-product-functions}

The following summarizes the major functions the system will perform:

* Customer account and saved-address management.  
* Product catalog browsing and product availability.  
* Standard ordering through cart and checkout.  
* Prepaid four-week subscriptions with deferment support.  
* Custom requests, cake configuration, and quotations.  
* QR Ph online payment processing.  
* Order and delivery status tracking.  
* Bill of Materials-based inventory and material planning.  
* Production capacity control and scheduling.  
* Cost-based pricing and product margin calculation.  
* Preparing-owner assignment and percentage allocation for each fulfillment product line.  
* Fulfilled-sales and recorded-payment analytics, including owner-attributed product sales, estimated production costs, and estimated profit.  
* Customer ratings, reviews, and administrative moderation.  
* Email, SMS, and internal notifications.  
* Role-Based Access Control for owners and staff.

## **2.3 User Classes and Characteristics** {#2.3-user-classes-and-characteristics}

| User Type | Technical Skill | Description | Key Capabilities |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| **Owner/Admin** | Basic to intermediate | Kitchen406 owners with full administrative access | Manage products, pricing, orders, subscriptions, custom cakes, inventory, capacity, deliveries, feedback, staff access, and notifications. Record and review preparing-owner allocations and view fulfilled-sales, recorded-payment, product-performance, and estimated-profit analytics. |
| **Staff** | Basic | Authorized bakery personnel responsible for operational tasks | View product and recipe information, record preparing owners and their allocation percentages, process orders, update permitted order statuses, view schedules and delivery information, manage permitted inventory records, and receive operational notifications. Access to financial analytics remains restricted to the Admin/Owner. |
| **Customer** | General public; browser literate | Registered customers using the Web Storefront | Browse products, manage addresses, place standard orders, enroll in subscriptions, request custom cakes, make payments, track orders and deliveries, receive notifications, and provide feedback. |
| **Guest** | General public; browser literate | Unregistered visitor | Browse publicly available products and information. Registration is required before completing transactions. |

## **2.4 Operating Environments** {#2.4-operating-environments}

* **Client side:** Web-based interface accessible through modern desktop and mobile browsers.  
* **Application:** Next.js, React, TypeScript, and Node.js.  
* **Database:** PostgreSQL with Prisma.  
* **Authentication:** Auth.js.  
* **Hosting:** Vercel for deployment and Railway for hosting PostgreSQL database and supporting background processes.  
* **External services:** Google Maps Platform, PayMongo, Lalamove, Brevo, Semaphore, and Cloudinary.  
* **Connectivity:** Internet connection required; no offline mode is specified.  
* **Market/currency**: Philippine market only, Philippine Peso (PHP) only.

## **2.5 Design and Implementation Constraints** {#2.5-design-and-implementation-constraints}

* The system shall be implemented as a web-based platform; no dedicated native mobile application is included.  
* All customer transactions shall require a registered account. Guest checkout is not supported.  
* Online payment shall use QR Ph through PayMongo, and payment must be confirmed before an order is finalized.  
* The system shall support three purchasing workflows: Standard Orders, Prepaid Subscriptions, and Custom Requests.  
* Subscriptions shall follow a prepaid four-week delivery cycle and shall not use automatic recurring billing.  
* Production shall be controlled by configurable capacity limits, scheduling rules, and blocked dates.  
* Inventory and costing shall use recipe and Bill of Materials data linked to products and configurable custom-cake components. The current design distinguishes projected requirements, reservations, and actual inventory movements.  
* Access shall be controlled by user role. Owners have administrative access, while staff access is restricted to approved operational functions such as order fulfillment and inventory-related activities.  
* Delivery and location functions depend on Google Maps Platform and Lalamove for supported delivery workflows.  
* The system shall not require integration with specialized hardware such as POS terminals, barcode scanners, or kitchen display systems.  
* The accuracy of pricing, inventory, capacity, and other operational outputs depends on the data configured and maintained by the owners.

## **2.6 Assumptions and Dependencies** {#2.6-assumptions-and-dependencies}

* Users are assumed to have access to a stable internet connection and a modern web browser.  
* Customers are assumed to provide valid account, contact, address, and transaction information.  
* Owners and authorized staff are responsible for maintaining accurate product, recipe, ingredient-cost, inventory, capacity, and scheduling data.  
* The system depends on the availability and continued compatibility of PayMongo, Google Maps Platform, Lalamove, Brevo, Semaphore, and Cloudinary.  
* The owners are assumed to maintain the accounts, credentials, API access, credits, and subscriptions required by the third-party services used by the platform.  
* Payment confirmation depends on PayMongo successfully processing and reporting the QR Ph transaction.  
* Delivery quotation, booking, and tracking functions depend on Lalamove availability within the bakery's supported service area.  
* System-generated inventory requirements, costing, and production schedules depend on correctly defined recipes, Bill of Materials records, stock information, and capacity settings.

# **3\. External Interface Requirements** {#3.-external-interface-requirements}

## **3.1 User Interfaces** {#3.1-user-interfaces}

![][image37]

Figure 1\. Product Catalog

This interface displays the available Kitchen406 products in a browsable catalog, including product image, category, name, variant information, price, availability status, and subscription eligibility where applicable. Customers may filter products by category, search the catalog, and limit results to subscription-eligible products before opening a product detail page. While catalog data is loading, the interface shall display a loading state or placeholder product cards. If products cannot be retrieved, the page shall display an error message with an option to retry, while unavailable products shall remain visible but clearly marked as temporarily unavailable. 

![][image38]

Figure 2\. Product Details

This interface displays the selected product’s image, category, name, description, price, available variant, availability status, quantity controls, and Add to Cart action. Products eligible for subscription are identified separately and provide a link to the subscription plans while remaining available for standard purchase. While product data is loading, the page shall display a loading state and temporarily disable purchase controls. If the product cannot be loaded or an Add to Cart action fails, the interface shall display a clear error message and allow the user to retry. 

![][image39]

Figure 3\. Customer Reviews

This interface presents verified feedback from completed Kitchen406 orders, including the overall rating, rating distribution, individual customer ratings, purchased product, written comments, optional review images, and submission date. Unauthenticated users are prompted to sign in before submitting a review, while review eligibility is verified against completed purchases. Figure 4\. Sign In Modal

This interface allows existing users to sign in using their registered email address and password, with controls for showing or hiding the password, recovering a forgotten password, and navigating to account registration. During authentication, the Sign In action shall indicate that the request is being processed and prevent repeated submissions. Figure 5\. Sign Up Modal

This interface allows a new customer to create a Kitchen406 account by providing their first name, last name, email address, Philippine mobile number, password, and password confirmation. Password visibility controls are provided, and successful registration proceeds to email verification before the account becomes active. While registration is being processed, the Create Account action shall indicate a loading state and prevent duplicate submissions. Invalid, incomplete, duplicate, or failed registration attempts shall display clear field-level or form-level error messages while preserving valid entered information. 

![][image42]

Figure 6\. Email Verification Modal

This interface allows a newly registered customer to verify their email address by entering the six-digit verification code sent to the registered email. The interface displays the code expiration time and provides an option to request a new code when necessary. Invalid, expired, or failed verification attempts shall display an appropriate error message and allow the customer to retry or request another code.

This interface allows a user who cannot access their account to request password-reset instructions by entering their registered email address. After submission, the system sends the applicable reset instructions to the provided email and allows the user to return to the Sign In interface. While the request is being processed, the Send Reset Link action shall display a loading state and prevent duplicate requests. Invalid email input or failed reset requests shall display a clear error message, while the response should avoid unnecessarily revealing whether a particular email address is registered.

This interface displays the products currently added to the customer’s cart, including the selected variant, quantity, individual price, and controls for changing quantity or removing an item. If the cart cannot be retrieved or updated, the interface shall display a clear error message and allow the customer to retry.

Before preparation begins, each product line shall have a valid preparing-owner allocation. Confirmation dialogs shall display the saved selections and permit changes while the allocation remains editable. Missing or invalid allocations shall prevent the affected order from progressing. Figure 35\. Production / Order Details

This interface presents the selected order’s products, quantities, fulfillment schedule, ingredient requirements, reserved quantities, available stock, shortages, and production history. Starting preparation and completing a pickup require confirmation of ingredient consumption or handover, respectively. While information or updates are processing, the interface shall indicate progress. Missing recipes, material shortages, unavailable records, or conflicting changes shall display clear messages and prevent invalid actions.

The interface shall provide a preparing-owner editor for each product line. Authorized Staff or an Admin/Owner may select Owner A, Owner B, or both owners. Selecting both owners shall initially propose an equal split and permit a whole-number percentage from 1 to 99 for Owner A, with Owner B receiving the remainder. An Apply to all products action shall copy the owner selection within the fulfillment. When both owners are selected, existing line percentages shall be retained and displayed for review. The editor shall show when allocations are locked and shall identify incomplete selections. Staff shall see the operational assignment information without access to calculated owner earnings.

Figure 55\. Reports and Analytics

This interface provides the Admin/Owner with separate Fulfilled sales and Recorded payments views. The default view shall show Fulfilled sales for the current month to date, with all owners, products, and order types included. The Admin/Owner may filter by reporting period, product, and order type. The Fulfilled sales view shall additionally support filtering by Owner A, Owner B, or Unallocated.

Fulfilled sales shall use the actual completion date and exclude delivery fees. It shall display allocated product sales, estimated profit, average purchase value, units or allocated units, sales trends, sales by order type, and leading products. Recorded payments shall use successful payment dates. Its product-revenue card and estimated-profit calculation shall use product amounts excluding delivery fees. When no product filter is applied, its payment trend, payment breakdown by order type, and average payment shall include the full recorded payment amounts, including delivery fees. When products are selected, these calculations shall use only the selected products’ amounts and exclude delivery fees. Labels and explanatory text shall identify the basis of the amounts displayed. Top products shall be ranked by product sales excluding delivery fees. Preparing-owner filters shall be unavailable in Recorded payments.

Missing required cost data shall display estimated profit as Unavailable while retaining the sales amount. Historical completed items without preparing-owner allocations shall remain visible as Unallocated. While information is loading, the interface shall display a loading state. Retrieval failures shall provide an error message and retry option, and filters without matching records shall display an informative empty state. Access shall remain restricted to the Admin/Owner.

New staff accounts shall be associated with the administrator who created them and assigned only the permitted staff functions. Deactivated accounts shall be prevented from accessing the staff interface. While records or account changes are processing, repeated submissions shall be prevented. Invalid account information, duplicate email addresses, or unsuccessful updates shall display clear messages and allow correction or retry.

This interface displays the Admin/Owner’s name, email address, contact number, and assigned role. It provides actions for editing permitted profile information, changing the password, and changing the login email address through the applicable verification process. Password changes shall require the current password and matching new-password entries, while email changes shall take effect only after successful verification. While profile or security updates are processing, the interface shall indicate progress and prevent repeated submissions. Invalid information, incorrect passwords, or unsuccessful verification shall display clear messages, while successful changes shall provide confirmation and failed updates shall allow correction or retry.

## **3.2 Hardware Interfaces** {#3.2-hardware-interfaces}

The system does not integrate with any hardware peripherals. No POS terminals, kitchen display systems, barcode scanners, or printers are required or supported. All interactions occur through a standard web browser on any internet-connected device.

## **3.3 Software Interfaces** {#3.3-software-interfaces}

| Interface | Purpose | Data Exchanged |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| **PostgreSQL Database** | Store the platform's accounts, products, orders, subscriptions, custom cake requests, inventory, recipes, payments, notifications, feedback, and other system records. | Application data through Prisma database operations |
| **Google Maps Platform** | Support address search, map display, location validation, and route/distance calculations. | Address queries, place information, coordinates, route and distance data |
| **PayMongo API v2** | Process QR Ph payments and obtain payment status information. | Payment amount, transaction reference, QR Ph payment information, and payment status |
| **Lalamove API v3** | Obtain delivery quotations, create supported delivery bookings, and receive delivery status information. | Pickup/drop-off locations, delivery details, quotation data, booking information, and delivery status |
| **Semaphore API v2.16** | Send SMS notifications to customers. | Recipient mobile number and notification message |
| **Brevo API** | Send email notifications generated by the system. | Recipient email address, subject, and notification content |
| **Cloudinary** | Store and retrieve images used by the platform. | Product images, custom-cake reference images, customer-review photos, and image URLs. |
| **Auth.js** | Provide authentication and session management for system users. | Authentication credentials, account/session information, and user role information |

## **3.4 Communications Interfaces** {#3.4-communications-interfaces}

* **EIR-COM-01:** All communication between the client application and the server shall occur through secure HTTPS connections.  
* **EIR-COM-02:** Communication between the Kitchen406 server and supported third-party APIs shall use HTTPS-based API requests.  
* **EIR-COM-03:** The system shall receive and process payment-status updates from PayMongo for QR Ph transactions.  
* **EIR-COM-04:** The system shall communicate with Lalamove to request delivery quotations, submit supported delivery bookings, and receive available delivery-status updates.  
* **EIR-COM-05:** The system shall communicate with Google Maps Platform to retrieve address, location, route, and distance information.  
* **EIR-COM-06:** The system shall send customer SMS notifications through the Semaphore API.  
* **EIR-COM-07:** The system shall send email notifications through the Brevo API.  
* **EIR-COM-08:** The system shall communicate with Cloudinary for the upload and retrieval of platform images.  
* **EIR-COM-09:** Third-party service credentials and API keys shall be handled on the server side and shall not be exposed through the customer-facing client application.

# **4\. System Features** {#4.-system-features}

## **4.1 Authentication and Access Control** {#4.1-authentication-and-access-control}

### **4.1.1 Description and Priority** {#4.1.1-description-and-priority}

This feature manages registration, authentication, account verification, password recovery, sessions, and role-based access for customers, staff, and administrators. **Priority: High.**

### **4.1.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.1.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When a new customer submits valid registration information, the system creates a customer account and associates it with a customer profile.  
* When a registered user submits valid login credentials, the system authenticates the account and provides access according to the user's assigned role.  
* When a user submits invalid login credentials, the system rejects the authentication attempt and displays an appropriate error message.  
* When a user requests password recovery, the system initiates the account-verification process before allowing the password to be changed.  
* When an authenticated staff user attempts to access an administrator-only function, the system denies access according to the configured role permissions.  
* When an authenticated user logs out, the system terminates the active session.

### **4.1.3 Functional Requirements** {#4.1.3-functional-requirements}

| ID | Requirement Description | Priority |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |

| FR-AUTH-03 | The system shall authenticate registered users using their account credentials. | High |
| FR-AUTH-04 | The system shall support customer, staff, and administrator access roles. | High |
| FR-AUTH-05 | The system shall restrict functions according to the authenticated user's role. | High |
| FR-AUTH-06 | The system shall provide an account-verification and password-recovery process. | High |
| FR-AUTH-07 | The system shall prevent staff users from accessing functions reserved for administrators. | High |

## **4.8 Subscription Management** {#4.8-subscription-management}

### **4.8.1 Description and Priority** {#4.8.1-description-and-priority}

This feature manages Kitchen406's prepaid subscription workflow consisting of four scheduled deliveries. **Priority: High.**

### **4.8.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.8.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When a customer selects an eligible subscription offering, the system displays the applicable subscription schedule and transaction information.  
* When a customer selects a subscription schedule, the system checks the required production capacity before the subscription commitment is finalized.  
* When the customer successfully completes the payment, the system creates four scheduled delivery records, confirms their capacity allocations, and retains the first fulfillment's ingredient reservation. Ingredient requirements for later fulfillments remain projected until their respective reservation dates.  
* When a prepaid subscription is confirmed, the system apportions the actual prepaid product amount across its four fulfillment orders using the original quantity and selling-price snapshots. Delivery fees are excluded from these product amounts.  
* When an authorized user opens a subscription fulfillment for preparation, the system allows preparing-owner allocations to be recorded independently of the other weekly fulfillments.  
* When a subscription fulfillment is completed, its apportioned product amount enters Fulfilled sales using its actual completion date. The original prepaid purchase remains the payment source and is counted only once in Recorded payments.  
* When a subscription delivery is completed, the system updates the delivery record and the subscription's remaining fulfillments.  
* When a customer submits a deferment request before the affected fulfillment’s preparation day begins, the system checks capacity for the next-day date and the date one week after the subscription’s final scheduled fulfillment. It offers only dates with sufficient capacity. If the customer confirms one offered date and the deferment allowance is unused, the system automatically reschedules the affected fulfillment and records the replacement allocation. If neither date has sufficient capacity, the system rejects the request and retains the original schedule and allowance.  
* When a subscription delivery is deferred, the system preserves the original delivery and capacity information rather than overwriting the previous record.  
* When a customer views an active subscription, the system displays its delivery schedule, completed deliveries, remaining deliveries, and applicable status information.

### **4.8.3 Functional Requirements** {#4.8.3-functional-requirements}

| ID | Requirement Description | Priority |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| FR-SUB-01 | The system shall allow registered customers to enroll in available subscription offerings. | High |
| FR-SUB-02 | The system shall require full prepaid payment for the four-week subscription. | High |
| FR-SUB-03 | The system shall create four scheduled subscription delivery records for each successful subscription. | High |
| FR-SUB-04 | The system shall track the remaining and completed subscription deliveries. | High |
| FR-SUB-05 | The system shall preserve the agreed preparation and fulfillment schedules of confirmed subscriptions, preventing subsequent changes to administrative schedule configurations from affecting existing commitments. | High |
| FR-SUB-06 | The system shall allow customers to request deferment of an upcoming, unfulfilled subscription delivery. | High |
| FR-SUB-07 | A deferred delivery shall be rescheduled without reducing the customer's total number of deliveries. | High |
| FR-SUB-08 | The system shall maintain the original and replacement capacity allocations associated with a deferment. | High |
| FR-SUB-09 | The system shall limit each subscription to one confirmed deferment. Rejected or ineligible requests shall not consume the allowance. | High |
| FR-SUB-10 | The system shall automatically apply a deferment after the customer confirms an offered replacement date with sufficient capacity, provided the request is timely and the deferment allowance is unused. Manual Admin/Owner approval is not required. | High |
| FR-SUB-11 | The system shall retain the original delivery schedule and deferment allowance when a request is rejected or cannot be accommodated. | High |
| FR-SUB-12 | The system shall accept deferment requests only before the configured preparation day of the affected fulfillment begins. | High |
| FR-SUB-13 | The system shall check only two deferment replacement dates. The next day and one week after the subscription’s final scheduled fulfillment.  | High |
| FR-SUB-14 | The system shall offer a date only when that date has sufficient production capacity and shall not search for a later replacement date. | High |
| FR-SUB-15 | The system shall preserve each fulfillment item’s share of the actual prepaid product amount using the original quantity and selling-price snapshots. Delivery fees shall be excluded. | High |
| FR-SUB-16 | The system shall permit independent preparing-owner allocations for each weekly fulfillment and shall include its product amount in Fulfilled sales only after that fulfillment is completed. | High |
| FR-SUB-17 | The system shall count the prepaid subscription payment once in Recorded payments and shall prevent the fulfillment orders from creating duplicate payment totals. | High |
| FR-SUB-18 | The system shall ensure that the apportioned fulfillment amounts total the original prepaid product amount after consistent currency rounding. A deferment shall preserve the affected fulfillment’s product amount. | High |

## **4.10 Checkout and Payment Management** {#4.10-checkout-and-payment-management}

### **4.10.1 Description and Priority** {#4.10.1-description-and-priority}

This feature validates a transaction before submission and processes full online payment through PayMongo QR Ph. **Priority: High.**

### **4.10.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.10.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When a customer proceeds to checkout, the system verifies that the customer is authenticated before allowing the transaction to continue.  
* When a customer reviews the checkout page, the system displays the selected items, applicable prices, fulfillment information, and transaction total.  
* When a customer selects a fulfillment schedule, the system validates the applicable inventory, capacity, blocked-date, cut-off, and scheduling requirements before payment.  
* When a customer selects delivery, the system validates the selected delivery address and obtains the applicable delivery quotation for the supported workflow.  
* When all checkout requirements are satisfied, the system calculates the final amount payable and allows the customer to proceed to QR Ph payment.  
* When payment begins, the system creates a 30-minute PayMongo QR Ph session and a 32-minute checkout hold.  
* When full payment is verified before hold expiration, the system confirms the order and retains its reservations.  
* When payment remains unconfirmed at hold expiration, the system checks its status with PayMongo.  
* When payment fails, expires, or remains unresolved after verification, the system cancels the order and releases reservations.  
* When payment is verified after reservation release, the system rechecks the transaction’s applicable ingredient requirements, production capacity, blocked dates, and scheduling constraints using the original fulfillment details. The system confirms the order only if all requirements remain satisfied and the necessary resources are successfully reserved again. Otherwise, the order remains cancelled, and the payment is recorded as eligible for an external refund.  
* When payment status changes, the system updates the associated transaction record for confirmation or reconciliation.

### **4.10.3 Functional Requirements** {#4.10.3-functional-requirements}

| ID | Requirement Description | Priority |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| FR-PAY-01 | The system shall require a registered account before checkout can be completed. | High |
| FR-PAY-02 | The system shall validate applicable product, inventory, scheduling, and capacity requirements before payment. | High |
| FR-PAY-03 | The system shall calculate the total amount payable before payment begins. | High |
| FR-PAY-04 | The system shall use PayMongo QR Ph for online payment processing. | High |
| FR-PAY-05 | The system shall require verified full payment through PayMongo before confirming an order. | High |
| FR-PAY-06 | The system shall record payment statuses and verify unresolved transactions with PayMongo when the checkout hold expires. | High |
| FR-PAY-07 | The system shall cancel unconfirmed orders and release reservations for failed, expired, or unresolved payments after the checkout hold expires and payment-status verification is performed. If payment is subsequently verified as successful, the system shall revalidate the original transaction’s applicable ingredient requirements, production capacity, blocked dates, and scheduling constraints. The system shall confirm the order only after all requirements are satisfied and the necessary resources are successfully reserved again. Otherwise, the order shall remain cancelled, and the customer shall be notified that the payment is eligible for an externally handled refund. | High |
| FR-PAY-08 | The system shall maintain a 30-minute QR Ph payment session and a 32-minute checkout hold, including a two-minute allowance for payment confirmation. | High |

## **4.11 Production Capacity and Scheduling** {#4.11-production-capacity-and-scheduling}

### **4.11.1 Description and Priority** {#4.11.1-description-and-priority}

This feature manages the bakery’s configurable production limits and scheduling constraints for standard orders, subscriptions, and custom cakes. It prevents overbooking by validating requested fulfillment dates against the applicable capacity limits, blocked dates, cut-off times, and lead-time requirements before an order commitment is accepted. Production capacity is maintained separately for each purchasing workflow and may be adjusted by the Admin/Owner according to the bakery’s current operational capability. **Priority: High.**

### **4.11.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.11.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When a customer selects a fulfillment date during checkout, the system checks the date against the applicable production capacity, blocked dates, cut-off rules, and required lead time.  
* When a customer selects a date whose applicable capacity has already been reached, the system prevents the customer from proceeding with that date and requires another valid fulfillment date.  
* When customer selects a date that has been blocked by the Admin/Owner, the system prevents new bookings for that date.  
* When a customer begins checkout for an available fulfillment date, the system temporarily holds the required production capacity while the payment transaction is in progress.  
* When the customer successfully completes payment, the system converts the temporary capacity hold into a confirmed capacity allocation for the order.  
* When the checkout or payment transaction does not proceed, the system releases the temporarily held production capacity so that it becomes available for other transactions.  
* When an Admin/Owner modifies a capacity limit or scheduling restriction, the system applies the updated configuration when validating subsequent bookings.  
* When a subscription delivery or confirmed deferment requires a scheduled fulfillment date, the system validates the corresponding subscription capacity before allocating the delivery.

### **4.11.3 Functional Requirements** {#4.11.3-functional-requirements}

| ID | Requirement Description | Priority |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| FR-CAP-01 | The system shall maintain separate production-capacity limits for standard orders, subscription fulfillments, and custom cakes. | High |
| FR-CAP-02 | The system shall allow the Admin/Owner to configure the production-capacity limits applicable to standard orders, subscription fulfillments, and custom cakes. | High |
| FR-CAP-03 | The system shall evaluate production capacity according to the requested fulfillment date rather than the date on which the transaction is placed. | High |
| FR-CAP-04 | The system shall enforce the configured capacity limit for standard orders on a per-delivery-day basis. | High |
| FR-CAP-05 | The system shall support a default standard-order capacity of up to four product varieties per delivery day, with up to ten units per variety, subject to Admin/Owner configuration. | High |
| FR-CAP-06 | The system shall enforce subscription capacity on a weekly basis for each subscription product. | High |
| FR-CAP-07 | The system shall support a default subscription capacity of ten units per product per week, subject to Admin/Owner configuration. | High |
| FR-CAP-08 | The system shall temporarily reserve capacity separately for all four subscription fulfillments during checkout and confirm these allocations upon successful payment. | High |
| FR-CAP-09 | The system shall enforce a default custom-cake capacity of two cakes per week, with each accepted cake assigned to a different fulfillment date, subject to Admin/Owner configuration. | High |
| FR-CAP-10 | The system shall allow the Admin/Owner to designate dates as blocked and unavailable for new bookings. | High |
| FR-CAP-11 | The system shall prevent a customer from selecting a fulfillment date that has reached its applicable capacity limit or has been blocked. | High |
| FR-CAP-12 | The system shall enforce the configured cut-off times and mandatory lead-time requirements applicable to each supported order type. | High |
| FR-CAP-13 | The system shall allow the Admin/Owner to configure applicable capacity baselines and cut-off rules to reflect changes in the bakery’s operational capability. | High |
| FR-CAP-14 | The system shall temporarily reserve the applicable production capacity when a customer enters the payment stage of checkout. | High |
| FR-CAP-15 | The system shall confirm reserved capacity when full payment is verified before the checkout hold expires. | High |
| FR-CAP-16 | The system shall release temporary capacity reservations when checkout is cancelled, payment fails, or the 32-minute hold expires without verified payment, following a final PayMongo status check. | High |
| FR-CAP-17 | The system shall validate available capacity before confirming a subscription enrollment and before applying a deferment to either permitted replacement date. | High |
| FR-CAP-18 | The system shall prevent an order from being confirmed when the required production capacity is unavailable, even if all other checkout requirements can be satisfied. | High |
| FR-CAP-19 | The system shall enforce a 12:00 PM cutoff at least one day before standard-order fulfillment, subject to any earlier product-specific preparation deadline. | High |
| FR-CAP-20 | The system shall enforce a 12:00 PM subscription enrollment cutoff at least one day before the first scheduled preparation date, based on the product's configured lead time. | High |
| FR-CAP-21 | The system shall require custom cake requests to be submitted at least seven calendar days before the requested fulfillment date. Subsequent Admin/Owner review or approval shall not invalidate a timely submitted request, provided fulfillment remains feasible. | High |

## **4.12 Inventory Management** {#4.12-inventory-management}

### **4.12.1 Description and Priority** {#4.12.1-description-and-priority}

This feature manages Kitchen406’s ingredient stock and the inventory movements associated with restocking, order requirements, consumption, and manual adjustments. The system uses recipe and Bill of Materials information maintained elsewhere in the platform to determine the ingredients required by orders, project material consumption, reserve stock during checkout, update inventory as stock is consumed or replenished, and identify shortages that may affect product availability. Both the Admin/Owner and authorized Staff can perform routine inventory operations. **Priority: High.**

### **4.12.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.12.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When an Admin/Owner or Staff member opens the inventory records, the system displays the current recorded stock quantities of the bakery’s ingredients.  
* When a confirmed order requires ingredients, the system determines the required quantities using the applicable recipe or Bill of Materials and reflects the expected ingredient consumption in inventory planning.  
* When a customer enters checkout, the system temporarily reserves the ingredients required for standard orders, custom cakes, or the first subscription fulfillment.  
* When the customer successfully completes payment, the system retains the required stock allocation for the confirmed order.  
* One day before a subsequent subscription fulfillment's scheduled preparation date, the system attempts to reserve its required ingredients.  
* If insufficient stock prevents reservation, the system notifies the Admin/Owner and allows the reservation to be retried after restocking.  
* When the checkout or payment transaction expires or fails to proceed, the system releases the temporarily reserved ingredient quantities.  
* When an ingredient reaches its configured low-stock threshold, the system alerts the Admin/Owner that replenishment is required.  
* When a required ingredient becomes fully depleted, the system prevents affected products from being ordered while the required ingredient remains unavailable.  
* When an Admin/Owner or Staff member records newly purchased ingredients, the system increases the corresponding recorded stock and records the restocking movement.  
* When an Admin/Owner or Staff member finds a discrepancy between physical and recorded stock, the user records an inventory adjustment and the system updates the stock quantity while preserving the reason for the adjustment.  
* When ingredient stock is consumed, replenished, reversed, or adjusted, the system records the resulting inventory movement for traceability.  
* When an authorized accidental correction returns a fulfillment from Preparing to Confirmed, the system reverses its recorded preparation consumption, restores the corresponding recorded physical stock, and retains those quantities as reserved for that fulfillment.  
* When preparation subsequently starts again, the system records consumption against the restored reservation without duplicating the earlier consumption or reversal.

## **4.13 Recipe and Bill of Materials Management** {#4.13-recipe-and-bill-of-materials-management}

### **4.13.1 Description and Priority** {#4.13.1-description-and-priority}

This feature manages the recipe and Bill of Materials (BoM) definitions used to connect sellable products and configurable cake components to the raw ingredients required for production. The Admin/Owner maintains the ingredient requirements and quantities associated with product variations, while authorized Staff may view recipe details for production purposes without being permitted to modify the underlying recipes. Kitchen406 uses a single-level BoM structure in which finished products are linked directly to base ingredients rather than to separately tracked intermediate or prepared components. **Priority: High.**

### **4.13.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.13.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When an Admin/Owner opens the recipe information for a product variation, the system displays the ingredients and quantities currently associated with that variation.  
* When an Admin/Owner modifies the ingredient composition or required quantity of a product variation, the system updates the corresponding BoM definition.  
* When an Admin/Owner associates an ingredient with a configurable custom-cake option, the system stores the ingredient requirement so that the selected configuration can be included in material calculations.  
* When a confirmed or pending order requires a product variation, the system reads the associated BoM to determine the raw ingredients and quantities required for that order.  
* When a custom cake includes configured options, the system uses the corresponding ingredient mappings to determine their required materials.  
* When a Staff member views a recipe during production, the system displays the required ingredients and quantities but does not allow the Staff member to alter the recipe.  
* When a recipe is used for costing, the system makes the defined ingredient quantities and associated inventory cost data available to the pricing calculation.

### **4.13.3 Functional Requirements** {#4.13.3-functional-requirements}

## **4.14 Pricing and Costing Management** {#4.14-pricing-and-costing-management}

### **4.14.1 Description and Priority** {#4.14.1-description-and-priority}

This feature provides the Admin/Owner with cost-based pricing support derived from the bakery's own recipe and inventory data. The system calculates each product's estimated production cost from its ingredient and packaging costs together with a configurable utility-overhead value, applies the configured markup percentage to produce a suggested selling price, and displays the resulting estimated production cost and profit-margin information for owner review. The suggested price serves only as decision support and does not automatically replace the product's final selling price. **Priority: High.**

### **4.14.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.14.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When an Admin/Owner views the costing information for a product variation, the system calculates and displays its current production cost and suggested selling price.  
* When the cost of an ingredient used by a product changes, the system uses the updated cost data when calculating that product's production cost and suggested price.  
* When an Admin/Owner changes the general utility-overhead value, the system uses the updated value in subsequent pricing calculations for products that do not have an individual override.  
* When an Admin/Owner configures a product-specific utility-overhead value, the system uses the override instead of the general default when costing that product.  
* When an Admin/Owner changes the markup percentage, the system recalculates suggested prices using the updated markup.  
* When the system produces a suggested selling price, the Admin/Owner reviews the recommendation and decides whether to retain or change the product's final selling price.  
* When an Admin/Owner changes a final selling price, the system stores the selected selling price separately from the system-generated suggested price.

## **4.15 Order Fulfillment Management** {#4.15-order-fulfillment-management}

### **4.15.1 Description and Priority** {#4.15.1-description-and-priority}

This feature manages paid and confirmed standard orders, subscription fulfillments, and custom-cake orders through preparation and completion. Authorized Staff and Admin/Owner accounts record the preparing owners and their agreed percentages for each fulfillment product line. These allocations identify the owners credited for production independently of the account performing a status update.

Users may review and correct allocations while the fulfillment remains unlocked. The system locks allocations during an active or unresolved courier booking and after fulfillment completion. Actual pickup, courier delivery, or owner-managed cake handoff establishes the completion date used by Fulfilled sales. Registered customers may view their own fulfillment progress. Financial calculations and analytics remain restricted to the Admin/Owner. **Priority: High.**

### **4.15.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.15.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When a customer's payment is successfully confirmed, the system places the corresponding order into the confirmed-order workflow for production and fulfillment.  
* When a Staff member opens the active-order view, the system displays confirmed orders requiring preparation and their relevant fulfillment information.  
* When a Staff member checks the production schedule, the system displays the orders and fulfillments associated with upcoming scheduled dates.  
* When a Staff member opens an order, the system displays the product, quantity, fulfillment, and applicable preparation information required to complete the order.  
* When a Staff member opens a custom-cake order, the system displays the approved custom-cake details needed for preparation.  
* When preparation of an order progresses, an authorized Staff member updates its status and the system records the new fulfillment state.  
* When an order becomes ready, the system reflects the updated order status so that the customer and Admin/Owner can see that progress.  
* When an Admin/Owner opens order management, the system displays confirmed orders and their fulfillment progress.  
* When a registered customer views an order, the system displays the current order status together with the selected fulfillment date and fulfillment method.  
* When an order requiring delivery reaches the appropriate fulfillment stage, the order becomes available for the separate delivery-management process.  
* When an authorized user opens a fulfillment for preparation, the system displays preparing-owner selections and percentages for each product line.  
* When the user selects both owners, the system initially proposes 50% for each owner and allows a valid whole-number percentage adjustment.  
* When the user starts preparation, the system validates all allocations, the current order version, payment and status prerequisites, and material availability. Successful preparation records ingredient consumption.  
* When the user reviews actual production contributions, the system allows allocation changes while the fulfillment remains unlocked.  
* When the user marks an order ready, the system retains the saved allocations. Ready status does not create a fulfilled sale.  
* When a courier booking becomes active or unresolved, the system locks allocations. If the booking fails or is cancelled while the order remains incomplete, the system permits allocation review before another booking attempt.  
* When pickup, courier delivery, or owner-managed cake handoff is completed, the system records the completion timestamp and locks allocations.  
* When an allocation or status save fails or conflicts with a newer order version, the system retains the previously saved values and requires the user to review and retry.  
* When an Admin/Owner or Staff member requests correction of an accidental fulfillment status change, the system displays the permitted previous status and the effects of confirming the reversal.  
* When the user confirms a reversal from Preparing to Confirmed, the system reverses the ingredient consumption recorded for that preparation start and restores the corresponding quantities to reserved stock for the same fulfillment.  
* When the user confirms a reversal from Ready to Preparing, the system changes the fulfillment status without reversing ingredient consumption.  
* When the user confirms a reversal from Completed to Ready, the system removes the fulfillment from Fulfilled sales, retains the previous completion information in audit history, and updates any linked subscription progress.  
* When a correction is unauthorized, conflicts with the current order version, or is blocked by courier status, the system rejects it without changing saved records.  
* When the user cancels confirmation or the save fails, the system preserves the prior fulfillment and inventory state.

## **4.16 Delivery Management** {#4.16-delivery-management}

### **4.16.1 Description and Priority** {#4.16.1-description-and-priority}

This feature manages the delivery-related processes for standard orders and subscription fulfillments, including service-area verification, delivery-fee quotation, courier booking, and delivery-status tracking. Google Maps Platform is used to validate the selected delivery location and determine whether it falls within the bakery's serviceable area, while Lalamove provides delivery quotations, booking, and subsequent status updates. Courier booking is performed by the Admin/Owner only after an order is ready for delivery. Custom cake delivery is excluded from this feature because it is handled manually by the owners outside the system. **Priority: High.**

### **4.16.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.16.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When a customer selects delivery as the fulfillment method, the system uses the selected delivery address for location and delivery processing.  
* When a delivery address is selected during checkout, the system validates the location and determines whether it falls within Kitchen406's serviceable area.  
* When the delivery address is outside the serviceable area, the system prevents the customer from proceeding with delivery to that address.  
* When a customer proceeds with an eligible delivery order, the system requests a delivery quotation from Lalamove and includes the returned delivery fee in the order summary.  
* When payment for a delivery order is completed, the system stores the required delivery information with the confirmed order without immediately booking a courier.  
* When an applicable standard order or subscription fulfillment is paid and ready, the Admin/Owner may initiate Lalamove booking after the system validates the preparing-owner allocations. The system locks allocations while the booking is pending, booked, in transit, or unresolved.  
* When Lalamove reports a delivery-status change, the system updates the corresponding delivery status.  
* When Lalamove reports Delivered, the system completes the associated fulfillment and records its completion timestamp.  
* When a courier booking fails or is cancelled while the order remains incomplete, the system permits allocation review and rebooking. The booking failure or cancellation does not automatically cancel or refund the customer’s payment.  
* When a  customer views an order with an active Lalamove delivery, the system displays the latest delivery status received from Lalamove.  
* When a custom cake becomes ready for delivery, no courier booking is performed by the system because custom cake delivery is handled independently by the owners.

### **4.16.3 Functional Requirements** {#4.16.3-functional-requirements}

## **4.17 Notification Management** {#4.17-notification-management}

### **4.17.1 Description and Priority** {#4.17.1-description-and-priority}

This feature manages automated customer and internal system notifications generated by relevant events within Kitchen406. Customer communications are delivered through Brevo for email and Semaphore for SMS, while internal system notifications may be presented to authorized administrative or staff users. The system also maintains records of outgoing notifications, their associated activity, provider, and sending status to reduce the need for repetitive manual customer messaging. **Priority: High.**

### **4.17.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.17.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When an order is successfully confirmed, the system sends the applicable order-confirmation notification to the customer.  
* When an order status changes at a notification-relevant stage, the system sends the applicable update to the customer.  
* When Lalamove reports a delivery-status change, the system sends the applicable delivery update to the customer.  
* When a scheduled subscription delivery is approaching, the system sends the applicable subscription reminder to the customer.  
* When an order or schedule change affects Staff operations, the system creates an internal system notification for the applicable staff users.  
* When an external notification is sent, the system records the notification type, provider, sending status, recipient context, and associated system activity.  
* When delivery of an external notification encounters an issue, the system retains the applicable sending and retry information in the notification record.

### **4.17.3 Functional Requirements** {#4.17.3-functional-requirements}

| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| FR-NOTIF-01 | The system shall automatically generate notifications when predefined notification-relevant events occur. | High |
| FR-NOTIF-02 | The system shall use Brevo to send applicable email notifications to customers. | High |
| FR-NOTIF-03 | The system shall use Semaphore to send applicable SMS notifications to customers. | High |
| FR-NOTIF-04 | The system shall send an order-confirmation notification after an order is successfully confirmed. | High |
| FR-NOTIF-05 | The system shall send applicable notifications when an order status changes. | High |
| FR-NOTIF-06 | The system shall send applicable notifications when a delivery status changes. | High |
| FR-NOTIF-07 | The system shall support notifications for upcoming subscription deliveries. | High |
| FR-NOTIF-08 | The system shall support internal system notifications for administrative or Staff users when relevant operational events affect their work. | Medium |
| FR-NOTIF-09 | The system shall associate an internal notification with its intended recipient role and related system activity. | Medium |
| FR-NOTIF-10 | The system shall maintain the read status of internal notifications independently for each recipient account. | Medium |
| FR-NOTIF-11 | The system shall maintain a log of outgoing external notifications. | High |
| FR-NOTIF-12 | The notification log shall record the notification type, delivery provider, sending status, and associated system record or activity. | Medium |
| FR-NOTIF-13 | The system shall retry failed email and SMS notifications up to three times, at intervals of 5, 15, and 30 minutes after each preceding failure.  | Medium |
| FR-NOTIF-14 | The system shall associate outgoing notifications with the applicable recipient account or recipient context. | Medium |
| FR-NOTIF-15 | If all retries fail, the system shall mark the notification as Failed, alert the Admin/Owner, and allow manual retry. | Medium |

## **4.18 Customer Review Management** {#4.18-customer-review-management}

### **4.18.1 Description and Priority** {#4.18.1-description-and-priority}

This feature allows registered customers to submit feedback for products they have actually purchased and allows the Admin/Owner to moderate submitted reviews. A review is associated with a specific purchased order item and includes a rating, an optional written comment, and up to three optional photos. Administrative moderation is manual; the owners may hide or unhide inappropriate feedback and record the reason for moderation. **Priority: Medium.**

### **4.18.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.18.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When a registered customer views a completed purchase, the system identifies purchased items that are eligible for feedback.  
* When a customer attempts to review a product they did not purchase, the system prevents the feedback submission.  
* When a customer submits feedback for an eligible purchased item, the system records the rating and any optional comment or uploaded photos.  
* When a customer attempts to submit another review for the same purchased order item, the system prevents the duplicate feedback submission.  
* When a customer attaches review photos, the system accepts up to three images for that feedback entry.  
* When an Admin/Owner opens customer feedback, the system displays submitted feedback for administrative review.  
* When an Admin/Owner determines that a review is inappropriate, the owner hides the feedback and specifies the applicable moderation reason.  
* When an Admin/Owner restores previously hidden feedback, the system makes the feedback visible again.

### **4.18.3 Functional Requirements** {#4.18.3-functional-requirements}

| ID | Requirement Description | Priority |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| FR-REV-01 | The system shall allow a registered customer to submit feedback only for an item from a completed order associated with that customer. | High |
| FR-REV-02 | The system shall prevent customers from submitting feedback for products they have not purchased. | High |
| FR-REV-03 | The system shall allow at most one feedback record for each purchased order item. | High |
| FR-REV-04 | The system shall require a rating when a customer submits feedback. | High |
| FR-REV-05 | The system shall allow the customer to include an optional written comment with a rating. | Medium |
| FR-REV-06 | The system shall allow the customer to attach up to three optional photos to a feedback entry. | Medium |
| FR-REV-07 | The system shall associate submitted feedback with the corresponding purchased order item. | High |
| FR-REV-08 | The system shall allow the Admin/Owner to view feedback submitted by customers. | High |
| FR-REV-09 | The system shall allow the Admin/Owner to hide customer feedback that is considered inappropriate for display. | High |
| FR-REV-10 | The system shall allow the Admin/Owner to unhide previously hidden feedback. | Medium |
| FR-REV-11 | The system shall require or record a moderation reason when feedback is hidden. | Medium |
| FR-REV-12 | The system shall support moderation reasons including spam, abusive language, off-topic content, sexual content, and another specified reason. | Medium |
| FR-REV-13 | The system shall record the Admin/Owner responsible for a feedback-moderation action. | Medium |
| FR-REV-14 | The system shall rely on manual Admin/Owner moderation and shall not automatically classify feedback using sentiment analysis, profanity filtering, or automated dispute resolution. | Medium |

## **4.19 Reports and Analytics** {#4.19-reports-and-analytics}

### **4.19.1 Description and Priority** {#4.19.1-description-and-priority}

This feature provides the Admin/Owner with Sales Analytics using separate Fulfilled sales and Recorded payments reporting bases. Fulfilled sales reports paid operational orders that have been completed and uses each fulfillment’s actual completion date. Recorded payments reports successful payments using their actual paid dates, including prepaid purchases whose fulfillments occur later.

For Fulfilled sales, the system uses the preparing-owner percentages recorded for each product line to calculate owner-attributed product sales, estimated costs, and estimated profit. The feature applies to standard orders, custom cakes, and individual weekly subscription fulfillments. Delivery fees are excluded from product-sales allocation.

Estimated profit is calculated using current recipe, ingredient-cost, packaging, and utility-overhead information. Changes to these inputs may change estimates displayed for earlier transactions. The feature provides reporting information without automatically transferring funds to owners, processing refunds, administering payroll, or producing complete accounting profit. 

In Recorded payments, product revenue and estimated profit shall exclude delivery fees. With all products included, payment charts and average payment shall use the full recorded payment amounts, including delivery fees. Applying a product filter shall limit these calculations to the selected products’ amounts and exclude delivery fees. The interface shall identify these differences through appropriate labels and explanatory text. **Priority: High.**

### **4.19.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences** {#4.19.2-stimulus/response-sequences}

* When an Admin/Owner opens Sales Analytics, the system displays Fulfilled sales for the current month to date with all owners, products, and order types included.  
* When the Admin/Owner switches the reporting basis, the system selects the corresponding records and uses completion dates for Fulfilled sales or paid dates for Recorded payments.  
* When the Admin/Owner selects a period, product, or order type, the system recalculates the applicable metrics and charts.  
* When the Admin/Owner applies a product filter in Recorded payments, the system recalculates the displayed amounts using only the selected products and excludes delivery fees. When the product filter is cleared, payment charts and average payment return to using the full recorded payment amounts. Product revenue and estimated profit continue to use product amounts excluding delivery fees.  
* When the Admin/Owner selects a preparing owner in Fulfilled sales, the system applies the stored product-line percentages to sales, estimated costs, and quantities.  
* When a paid fulfillment is completed, the system includes its product amounts in Fulfilled sales for the completion period.  
* When a subscription fulfillment is completed, the system includes only that fulfillment’s apportioned product amount. The original prepaid payment remains recorded once in Recorded payments.  
* When the Admin/Owner selects Unallocated, the system displays eligible historical completed items without recorded owner allocations.  
* When required cost information is missing, the system retains the sales figure and displays the affected estimated profit as Unavailable.  
* When an authorized reversal makes a fulfillment incomplete, the system removes it from Fulfilled sales. A later valid completion includes it once using the new completion timestamp.  
* When the Admin/Owner clears filters, the system restores the default reporting settings.  
* When a Staff member attempts to access Sales Analytics, the system denies access.

## **4.19.3 Functional Requirements** {#4.19.3-functional-requirements}
